metadata.title: Links Switches and Routers
metadata.subject: NCC — Net-Centric Computing
metadata.contentType: Original practice based on the accompanying lecture notes

questions.question: Which information does an Ethernet learning switch record from an incoming frame?
options: A) The destination SMTP mailbox and password
B) The TCP sequence number as an IP route
C) The DNS MX preference as a port
D) The source MAC and ingress port within the VLAN
questions.explanation: Switch learning associates observed source interfaces with reachable ports.

source.section: Section 11 — Switches routers and a packet journey

questions.question: What happens to an unknown unicast destination on a conventional learning switch?
options: A) It is broadcast through every router on the Internet
B) The switch always drops it without learning
C) It is delivered to the SMTP process inside the switch
D) It is flooded to eligible ports in the same VLAN except the ingress port
questions.explanation: Flooding is scoped to the relevant bridged broadcast domain.

source.section: Section 11 — Switches routers and a packet journey

questions.question: What does an ordinary layer-2 switch do to the IP TTL while forwarding within one LAN?
options: A) It decreases the IP TTL by one
B) It resets the IP TTL to 64
C) It replaces the IP TTL with the DNS TTL
D) It leaves the IP TTL unchanged
questions.explanation: A bridge forwards frames without acting as an IP hop.

source.section: Section 11 — Switches routers and a packet journey

questions.question: What changes when R1 forwards a packet from its source LAN to the transit Ethernet link?
options: A) The SMTP envelope recipient at every router
B) The TCP sequence numbers under ordinary forwarding
C) The local frame source and destination MAC addresses
D) The remote destination IP under the no-NAT assumption
questions.explanation: The router terminates incoming link encapsulation and builds a frame for the outgoing link.

source.section: Section 11 — Switches routers and a packet journey

questions.question: Which address pair belongs to the R1-to-R2 transit frame?
options: A) A MAC to B MAC across the whole Internet
B) B MAC to A MAC because TCP is full duplex
C) R1 transit MAC to R2 transit MAC
D) R1 LAN MAC to the recipient email address
questions.explanation: Each routed link uses its own neighboring link interfaces.

source.section: Section 11 — Switches routers and a packet journey

questions.question: Why does the TCP checksum stay unchanged when only IPv4 TTL changes?
options: A) Every router disables TCP checking
B) TCP checksums are always zero
C) TTL is outside the TCP checksum coverage and pseudoheader
D) The SMTP process recalculates it at each router
questions.explanation: The IPv4 header checksum changes with TTL, while TCP protects different fields.

source.section: Section 11 — Switches routers and a packet journey

questions.question: What does Ethernet FCS primarily provide?
options: A) Detection of accidental frame corruption using a CRC
B) Encryption of SMTP message content
C) End-to-end acknowledgment of mailbox delivery
D) Resolution of domain names
questions.explanation: FCS is link-level error detection, not application acceptance or cryptographic protection.

source.section: Section 10 — Ethernet Wi Fi and the physical medium

questions.question: Which statement matches modern switched full-duplex Ethernet?
options: A) The link does not use the shared-medium collision behavior of old half-duplex Ethernet
B) Every packet must collide once before transmission
C) CSMA/CD is the central retry mechanism on every full-duplex port
D) Full duplex eliminates all switch queueing
questions.explanation: Dedicated full-duplex links avoid classic shared-medium collisions but can still experience congestion.

source.section: Section 10 — Ethernet Wi Fi and the physical medium

questions.question: Why does TCP reliability remain useful over a Wi-Fi link with local retries?
options: A) Wi-Fi acknowledgments prove the final SMTP transaction succeeded
B) Wi-Fi replaces all TCP sequence fields
C) Local retries can fail and do not cover the entire end-to-end path
D) A local retry always creates a new TCP connection
questions.explanation: Link recovery covers a local scope; TCP detects missing bytes across the connection path.

source.section: Section 10 — Ethernet Wi Fi and the physical medium

questions.question: In an ordinary station-to-AP three-address 802.11 frame, what does address 1 identify?
options: A) The recipient SMTP mailbox
B) The radio receiver and AP BSSID
C) The remote Internet server MAC across all routers
D) The TCP destination port
questions.explanation: The AP receiver address can differ from the final link destination represented by address 3.

source.section: Section 10 — Ethernet Wi Fi and the physical medium

questions.question: What can an access point do when bridging Wi-Fi to Ethernet?
options: A) Automatically act as the remote SMTP server
B) Change the link framing while carrying the same IP packet
C) Reduce the email Subject to an IPv4 address
D) Preserve all original 802.11 headers inside every ordinary Ethernet header
questions.explanation: Bridging translates local link encapsulation; routing is a distinct additional role.

source.section: Section 10 — Ethernet Wi Fi and the physical medium

questions.question: What is the ordinary untagged Ethernet header size before payload?
options: A) 4 bytes
B) 14 bytes
C) 20 bytes
D) 40 bytes
questions.explanation: Destination MAC 6 + source MAC 6 + EtherType 2 = 14 bytes.

source.section: Section 10 — Ethernet Wi Fi and the physical medium

questions.question: What does EtherType 0x0800 identify?
options: A) IPv4
B) ARP
C) IPv6
D) SMTP directly
questions.explanation: EtherType dispatches the Ethernet payload to the network-layer protocol.

source.section: Section 10 — Ethernet Wi Fi and the physical medium

questions.question: What is the main distinction between transmission and propagation delay?
options: A) Transmission is measured in MAC addresses; propagation in SMTP commands
B) A higher bit rate reduces both by exactly the same factor
C) Both are determined only by the DNS cache
D) Transmission serializes bits; propagation is travel through the medium
questions.explanation: Bit rate affects serialization; distance and signal speed affect propagation.

source.section: Section 10 — Ethernet Wi Fi and the physical medium

questions.question: Which device state maps IP prefixes to forwarding actions?
options: A) A router forwarding table
B) A switch MAC forwarding database
C) An SMTP mail queue
D) A DNS MX cache
questions.explanation: Different tables solve different parts of the end-to-end delivery problem.

source.section: Section 11 — Switches routers and a packet journey

questions.question: Why can two hosts on different VLANs require routing even on one physical switch?
options: A) The switch must rewrite every SMTP From header
B) The VLANs separate broadcast domains and IP-subnet forwarding requires a routing function
C) Each VLAN uses a unique universal TCP sequence number
D) DNS is disabled between ports on one switch
questions.explanation: A physical box can implement several logical layer functions, including routing between VLANs.
